messages:
Maria Chen: Hey sec — prepping Private deployment onboarding for a customer who will use GCP Cloud KMS in their project. Need short, pragmatic guidance on: (1) service account / IAM bindings (key vs keyRing vs project), (2) audit logging/export for KMS calls, (3) envelope-encryption best practices (DEK caching TTLs, rewrap on KEK rotation), and (4) emergency rotation runbook. TL;DR: want minimal perms for runtime + safe rotation. Any gotchas?

Samir Patel: +1. High-level guidance: 1) Create a dedicated SA per-customer (eg redwood-kms-access@cust-project). 2) Grant the SA roles on the specific cryptoKey (not wide project role). Prefer roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter (or separate encrypter + decrypter roles if you want stricter split). 3) If our control plane needs to impersonate that SA, give the control-plane SA roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the customer SA (scoped to that SA).

Example gcloud snippets we use in templates:
```
# grant runtime SA decrypt rights on a single key
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding \
  projects/PROJECT/locations/LOCATION/keyRings/KEYRING/cryptoKeys/KEY \
  --member=serviceAccount:redwood-kms-access@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter

# allow control-plane to impersonate the per-customer SA
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding \
  redwood-kms-access@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --member=serviceAccount:control-plane@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator
```

Samir Patel: Notes: - Bind at cryptoKey level whenever possible (key-level binding). - Don't give broad project-level roles like roles/cloudkms.admin unless strictly necessary. - If customers want to use Workload Identity / federated identities, we can support impersonation flows to avoid long-lived keys in our infra.

Jordan Lee: Audit / logging notes: Cloud Audit Logs: admin activity logs are enabled by default, but Data Access logs (which include KMS API calls like encrypt/decrypt) are often disabled by default and need explicit enablement or export configuration on the customer's project. We want those events forwarded to our observability stack (or customer's chosen SIEM) for: decrypt attempts, key version usage, failed IAM checks.

Quick sink example (customer grants our sink writer SA appropriate writer role on their target):
```
# create a sink that filters KMS audit events and writes to a BigQuery dataset (customer-project)
gcloud logging sinks create redwood-kms-audit \
  bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/OUR-OBSERVABILITY-PROJ/datasets/kms_audit \
  --log-filter='protoPayload.serviceName="cloudkms.googleapis.com"' \
  --project=customer-project
```
Then customer grants the sink's writer SA permissions on the destination dataset. Audit logs are essential for post-incident forensics and for detecting unexpected decrypt patterns.

Priya Rao: Envelope encryption + rotation pattern (recommended):
- Generate a unique DEK per-tenant (or per-resource) and use a strong symmetric algorithm (AES-GCM).
- DEKs are encrypted with the customer's KEK (Cloud KMS cryptoKey). Only the runtime SA can call KMS to unwrap (Decrypt) DEKs.
- Cache plaintext DEKs in memory only, with a short TTL. We typically recommend 1 hour by default and up to 6–12 hours only if absolutely necessary for latency/cost tradeoffs. Use an in-memory secure heap and zero memory on eviction.
- Rotation: when rotating the KEK, create a new key version (do not destroy old versions). Rewrap existing encrypted DEKs to the new key version by decrypting with old KEK and encrypting with new KEK (this is 'rewrap'). Perform rewrap as a background job; mark items as 'rewrap_pending' in the metadata so in-flight requests can fallback to decrypt with old key when needed. Only retire old key versions after rewrap completes + a safety grace period (e.g., 7 days).

Sample Terraform IAM binding (pattern):
```hcl
resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member" "runtime_decrypter" {
  crypto_key_id = "projects/${var.project}/locations/${var.location}/keyRings/${var.ring}/cryptoKeys/${var.key}"
  role          = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"
  member        = "serviceAccount:${var.runtime_sa_email}"
}
```

Priya Rao: Emergency rotation (runbook sketch):
1) Trigger: detected key compromise or leaked SA key material.
2) Immediately revoke runtime SA tokens / disable the SA (short-term) to stop new decrypts while we assess.
3) Create a new KEK version in the customer's key and mark as primary.
4) Start rewrap job: re-encrypt all stored DEKs with the new key version. Use small batches and monitor error rates. Keep old key versions active until rewrap verification completes.
5) Rotate any config pointers (if runtime uses key version aliases) and confirm successful decrypts in canary.
6) Re-enable SA / restore minimal runtime access.
7) Post-incident: run audit, rotate any credentials that may have been exposed, and extend monitoring for 72h.

Caveats: relying solely on destroying a key version to lock access can be destructive; prefer disabling SA or toggling IAM first and ensure you have a tested rewrap path before retiring keys.

sec-bot: Link to our internal runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-private-rotation (runbook includes scripts for rewrap worker, sink templates, and a checklist for customer on-boarding). Also: file an incident ticket and ping #oncall if this is a live compromise.

Maria Chen: This is perfect — I'll draft the onboarding checklist with the gcloud/terraform snippets and add the rewrap job to the deployment pipeline. Plan: default DEK TTL 1h, allow cust opt-in to 6h max, require KMS Data Access audit exports. Thanks all.
